_meta.categories: 3 multi-hop, 4 constraint, 5 negative/absence, 6 cross-border divergence, 7 hierarchy-traversal
_meta.ground_truth_source: Stage 4 data: bvl_{disease}_DE.json (BVL PSM API) + no_products.json (Mattilsynet labels)
_meta.disease_assignment: late blight = rich data (112 DE / 4 NO), carries heavy relational Qs; apple scab (9/1) moderate; powdery mildew (1/1) anchors negative/absence + cross-border showcase
_meta.status: Cross-border + absence answers VERIFIED against Stage-4 data (verify_benchmark_gt.py). Category 7 (hierarchy) still needs BVL kultur-code inspection.
_meta.confirmed_divergence: DE late blight: 22 active substances / 112 products vs NO: 4 substances / 4 products. DE-only substances incl. fluazinam, kupferhydroxid, cymoxanil. difenoconazole appears in NO (Revus Top) but not in DE late-blight data.
_meta.category_7_status: OPEN — hierarchy-traversal not yet instantiated. Requires inspecting whether BVL kultur (crop) codes in the late-blight data are hierarchical (parent group -> child crop). The three benchmark diseases (potato/tomato/apple/cucurbit) may lack a clear parent-child crop structure; if so, category 7 is marked not-applicable to this disease set rather than dropped silently. Decide during Stage 3 KG design.
_meta.normalisation_note: Substance names normalised across DE/NO/English spellings (src/substance_norm.py) before computing cross-border answers. difenoconazole is authorised in BOTH countries (earlier draft wrongly listed it as DE-only due to a spelling mismatch). True DE-only late-blight set = 18 substances.

category_3_multi_hop.q: Which active substances are used in Norway-authorised products against potato late blight?
category_3_multi_hop.answer: cyazofamid, mandipropamid, difenoconazole, oxathiapiprolin (from Ranman TOP, Revus, Revus Top, Revus Pro)

category_3_multi_hop.q: Which Germany-authorised active substance appears in a Norway-authorised late blight product too?
category_3_multi_hop.answer: cyazofamid, mandipropamid, difenoconazole, and oxathiapiprolin all appear in BOTH German and Norwegian late-blight products (confirmed after normalising substance-name spellings across the two sources — the German 'Difenoconazol' and Norwegian 'difenoconazole' are the same substance).

category_3_multi_hop.q: For late blight, which active substances are authorised in Germany but not in Norway?
category_3_multi_hop.answer: Germany authorises 18 active substances against late blight that Norway does not, including fluazinam, copper hydroxide, copper oxychloride, cymoxanil, azoxystrobin, ametoctradin, amisulbrom, and zoxamide. (Norway's 4 — cyazofamid, mandipropamid, difenoconazole, oxathiapiprolin — are all also authorised in Germany.)

category_3_multi_hop.q: Which crops are covered by Norway's authorised late blight products?
category_3_multi_hop.answer: potato only (all 4 NO late-blight products are for potato)

category_4_constraint.q: Which Norway-authorised late blight products contain mandipropamid?
category_4_constraint.answer: Revus, Revus Top, Revus Pro (Ranman TOP does not — it is cyazofamid)

category_4_constraint.q: Which Norway-authorised late blight product contains a single active substance (not a mixture)?
category_4_constraint.answer: Ranman TOP (cyazofamid) and Revus (mandipropamid); Revus Top and Revus Pro are mixtures

category_4_constraint.q: Which Norway late blight products combine mandipropamid with a second active substance?
category_4_constraint.answer: Revus Top (+ difenoconazole) and Revus Pro (+ oxathiapiprolin)

category_4_constraint.q: Is there a copper-based product authorised for late blight in Norway?
category_4_constraint.answer: No copper-based product is among Norway's 4 late-blight products; Germany authorises copper (kupferhydroxid — Cuprozin, Funguran). Confirmed divergence.

category_5_negative_absence.q: Is there more than one authorised product for cucurbit powdery mildew in Germany?
category_5_negative_absence.answer: No — exactly one (PODOXA scope). A definitive negative.

category_5_negative_absence.q: Is the German late blight product BANJO (fluazinam) authorised in Norway?
category_5_negative_absence.answer: No — fluazinam (BANJO) is authorised for late blight in Germany but is NOT among Norway's 4 authorised late-blight products. Confirmed absence.

category_5_negative_absence.q: Are copper-hydroxide products (e.g. Cuprozin) authorised for late blight in Norway?
category_5_negative_absence.answer: No — copper hydroxide (Cuprozin/Funguran) is authorised in Germany but not among Norway's late-blight products. Confirmed absence.

category_5_negative_absence.q: Is there an authorised apple-scab product in Norway other than Delan Pro?
category_5_negative_absence.answer: VERIFY: none other collected — Delan Pro is the only one found. A near-absence worth confirming.

category_6_cross_border_divergence.q: How does the number of authorised late-blight products differ between Germany and Norway?
For apple scab, how many products are authorised in each country?
Is the active substance cyazofamid (Ranman TOP) authorised against late blight in both Germany and Norway?
category_6_cross_border_divergence.answer: cyazofamid (Ranman TOP) is authorised against late blight in BOTH Germany and Norway. Confirmed present in both.

category_6_cross_border_divergence.q: A grower moves a potato operation from Germany to Norway. What changes about the range of authorised late-blight products available?
category_6_cross_border_divergence.answer: It narrows sharply — from 112 authorised German products to 4 in Norway; Norway actively restricts late-blight products.

category_6_cross_border_divergence.q: For cucurbit powdery mildew, how do the two countries compare?
category_6_cross_border_divergence.answer: Both authorise very few — Germany 1, Norway 1 (Talius). A rare case of parity, unlike late blight.

category_6_cross_border_divergence.q: For late blight, name an active substance authorised in Germany but not in Norway.
category_6_cross_border_divergence.answer: fluazinam, copper hydroxide, or cymoxanil — each authorised against late blight in Germany but absent from Norway's authorisations. In total 18 substances are DE-authorised but not NO-authorised (after cross-language name normalisation). NOTE: difenoconazole is NOT one of them — it is authorised in both countries.
